text.p: Here are the highlights of stories in the Danish press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
--Tax authorities are to repay 200 million crowns to doctors, taken from them in the form of improper deductions between 1998 and 1990.
--The banks and the Confederation of Danish Industries agree that Monday's trade figures indicate a new boom for industrial exports.
--Car sales are running at double their usual rate for the time of year, as motorists seek to buy new vehicles ahead of a June duty increase.
--The need for further fiscal tightening in 1997 has been greatly reduced by Monday's favourable trade and current account figures, says Finance Minister Mogens Lykketoft.
--Danish service businesses are increasingly expanding abroad, their foreign investments increased 10-fold between 1983 and 1995, export of services earned 10 billion crowns in 1996.
--The main opposition Liberal party intends to put the sale of the state's majority stake in Tele Danmark on the agenda for negotiations with the government on the 1998 budget.

--Pension fund LD says it does not plan to divest its holding in Cheminova, despite criticism of the firm's exports to the developing world of pesticides banned at home. LD says that following a meeting with Cheminova's management it is convinced that they are taking the problem seriously.
